name: Enhanced Due Diligence Policy
description: Policy mandating Enhanced Due Diligence procedures for high-risk customers. Establishes mandatory risk indicators triggering EDD, defines procedural requirements including senior staff approval, beneficial ownership investigation, source of funds verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring with quarterly reassessment.
context: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Mandatory for High-Risk Customers

EDD Procedures: 1. Senior staff approval required 2. Additional identity verification 3. Beneficial ownership investigation (if entity) 4. Source of funds verification 5. Enhanced ongoing monitoring 6. Quarterly risk reassessment 7. Documentation of risk assessment

name: Senior Staff Approval Requirement for High-Risk Customers
description: Mandatory requirement that senior staff approval must be obtained before proceeding with account opening or relationship establishment for customers identified as high-risk under EDD criteria.

name: Additional Identity Verification for High-Risk Customers
description: Requirement to conduct additional identity verification beyond standard KYC procedures for customers meeting high-risk indicators under the EDD policy.

name: Beneficial Ownership Investigation for Entity Customers

name: Source of Funds Verification

name: Enhanced Ongoing Monitoring for High-Risk Customers
description: Requirement to implement enhanced ongoing monitoring of high-risk customer accounts and transactions beyond standard monitoring procedures.

name: Quarterly Risk Reassessment for High-Risk Customers
description: Mandatory requirement to conduct and document risk reassessment of high-risk customers on a quarterly basis to determine if risk profile has changed.

name: Documentation of Risk Assessment
description: Requirement to document and retain records of all risk assessments conducted under the Enhanced Due Diligence policy for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Unclear Beneficial Ownership
description: Risk indicator where the beneficial ownership structure of a customer entity is unclear or opaque, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence requirements.

name: Weak AML Control Jurisdictions
description: Risk indicator identifying customers with connections to jurisdictions known to have weak Anti-Money Laundering controls, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence.

name: Politically Exposed Person Status
description: Risk indicator identifying customers who are Politically Exposed Persons or family members of PEPs, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence requirements.

name: Sanctions List Match
description: Risk indicator where a customer matches or potentially matches a sanctions list, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence and potential compliance escalation.

name: Adverse Media
description: Risk indicator where adverse media coverage or negative news is associated with a customer, triggering Enhanced Due Diligence requirements.

name: High-Value Account Risk
description: Risk indicator identifying accounts with high transaction values or balances, which may indicate elevated money laundering or financial crime risk.

name: Complex Transaction Patterns
description: Risk indicator identifying customers with unusual or complex transaction patterns that may indicate money laundering, terrorist financing, or other financial crime.

name: Non-Face-to-Face Relationship Risk
description: Risk indicator where the customer relationship is established or maintained without face-to-face contact, reducing verification capability and triggering Enhanced Due Diligence.

name: Enhanced Ongoing Monitoring System
description: Operational control implementing enhanced monitoring of high-risk customer transactions and account activity beyond standard monitoring procedures.

name: Beneficial Ownership Investigation Process
description: Operational control requiring investigation and documentation of beneficial ownership structures for entity customers identified as high-risk.

name: Source of Funds Verification Process
description: Operational control requiring verification and documentation of the source of funds for high-risk customers.

name: Quarterly Risk Reassessment Review
description: Operational control implementing quarterly review and reassessment of high-risk customer risk profiles with documented findings.

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance role with authority to approve Enhanced Due Diligence procedures and high-risk customer onboarding decisions under this policy.

name: Senior Staff
description: Senior staff members responsible for reviewing and approving Enhanced Due Diligence procedures and high-risk customer decisions as required by policy.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Identity Verification
description: Enhanced identity verification process applied to high-risk customers, including additional verification steps beyond standard KYC procedures.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification
description: Enhanced due diligence verification process to identify and confirm the beneficial owners of entity customers identified as high-risk.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customer classification for individuals or entities meeting one or more high-risk indicators under the Enhanced Due Diligence policy, requiring enhanced compliance procedures.

name: Transaction Monitoring Policy
description: A policy governing the detection and monitoring of suspicious transaction patterns indicative of money laundering or terrorist financing activities. The policy establishes the framework for identifying and responding to transactions that may indicate financial crime.
context: Detect suspicious transaction patterns indicative of money laundering or terrorist financing

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk of customer accounts and transactions being used to conceal the origins of illegally obtained funds. This is a primary focus of the transaction monitoring policy.
context: Detect suspicious transaction patterns indicative of money laundering or terrorist financing

name: Terrorist Financing
description: The risk of customer accounts and transactions being used to fund terrorist activities or organizations. This is a primary focus of the transaction monitoring policy.
context: Detect suspicious transaction patterns indicative of money laundering or terrorist financing

name: Transaction Monitoring System
description: An operational control mechanism designed to detect and flag suspicious transaction patterns that may indicate money laundering or terrorist financing. The system monitors transactions to identify anomalies and high-risk activities.
context: Detect suspicious transaction patterns indicative of money laundering or terrorist financing

name: Fraud Detection Engine
description: An automated system that monitors customer transactions against predefined rules to detect potential fraud. The engine generates alerts for large deposits, rapid movements, velocity patterns, geographic anomalies, high-risk jurisdictions, and unusual beneficiaries, triggering manual review or automatic blocking actions.
context: Large deposit | >£50,000 in 24h | Alert + manual review
High-risk jurisdiction | Transaction with sanctioned country | Auto-block

name: Large Deposit Alert
description: An automated monitoring rule that triggers an alert and manual review when a deposit exceeds £50,000 within a 24-hour period. This control is designed to identify potentially suspicious high-value deposit activity.
context: Large deposit | >£50,000 in 24h | Alert + manual review

name: Rapid Movement Alert
description: An automated monitoring rule that flags transactions where a deposit is followed by a withdrawal within less than 2 hours. This control detects potential layering or rapid fund movement patterns indicative of money laundering.
context: Rapid movement | Deposit then withdrawal <2h | Alert for review

name: Velocity Alert
description: An automated monitoring rule that generates a velocity alert when 10 or more transfers to different recipients occur within a 24-hour period. This control identifies potential structuring or rapid distribution patterns.
context: Multiple small transfers | 10+ transfers to different recipients <24h | Velocity alert

name: Geographic Anomaly Alert
description: An automated monitoring rule that triggers an alert for manual review when a transaction occurs in a different country within 2 hours of a previous transaction. This control detects geographically impossible or suspicious transaction patterns.
context: Geographic anomaly | Transaction in different country within 2 hours | Alert for review

name: High-Risk Jurisdiction Block
description: An automated control that automatically blocks transactions involving sanctioned countries or high-risk jurisdictions. This is a preventive measure that stops transactions before they complete rather than generating an alert.
context: High-risk jurisdiction | Transaction with sanctioned country | Auto-block

name: Unusual Beneficiary Alert
description: An automated monitoring rule that triggers an alert for manual review when a transfer is made to a new beneficiary above a defined threshold. This control identifies transfers to previously unknown recipients that may warrant additional scrutiny.
context: Unusual beneficiary | Transfer to new beneficiary >threshold | Alert for review

name: Manual Alert Review
description: A manual monitoring process performed by the Financial Crime team to review alerts generated by the automated fraud detection engine. The team conducts pattern analysis, behavioral profiling, and judgment-based assessment of suspicious activity.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The team responsible for reviewing fraud detection alerts, conducting pattern analysis for suspicious sequences, assessing behavioral profiling changes, and making judgment-based assessments of flagged transactions.

name: Large Deposit Risk
description: The risk that unusually large deposits (exceeding £50,000 in 24 hours) may indicate money laundering, fraud, or other financial crime activity requiring investigation.
context: Large deposit | >£50,000 in 24h | Alert + manual review

name: Rapid Fund Movement Risk
description: The risk that deposits followed immediately by withdrawals (within 2 hours) may indicate layering or rapid fund movement consistent with money laundering schemes.
context: Rapid movement | Deposit then withdrawal <2h | Alert for review

name: Structuring Risk
description: The risk that multiple small transfers to different recipients within a short timeframe (10+ transfers in 24 hours) may indicate structuring or deliberate fragmentation of funds to evade detection.
context: Multiple small transfers | 10+ transfers to different recipients <24h | Velocity alert

name: Geographic Anomaly Risk
description: The risk that transactions occurring in geographically distant locations within an impossibly short timeframe (2 hours) may indicate account compromise, fraud, or unauthorized access.
context: Geographic anomaly | Transaction in different country within 2 hours | Alert for review

name: Sanctions Violation Risk
description: The risk that transactions with sanctioned countries or high-risk jurisdictions may violate sanctions regulations and expose the bank to regulatory penalties and reputational harm.
context: High-risk jurisdiction | Transaction with sanctioned country | Auto-block

name: Unusual Beneficiary Risk
description: The risk that transfers to new or previously unknown beneficiaries above a defined threshold may indicate account compromise, fraud, or unauthorized fund diversion.
context: Unusual beneficiary | Transfer to new beneficiary >threshold | Alert for review

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk of customer accounts being used to disguise the origins of illicit funds through deposit and transfer patterns. The document identifies specific suspicious transaction patterns including large deposits followed by international transfers, round-dollar amounts to multiple countries, and structuring activities designed to evade reporting thresholds.
context: Large deposit immediately followed by international transfer
Structuring (repeated transfers just below reporting threshold)

name: Fraud
description: The risk of fraudulent activity detected through abnormal transaction patterns, including deposits made using different names or accounts and cash deposits followed by wire transfers out, which may indicate account compromise or unauthorized use.
context: Cash deposits followed by wire transfers out

name: Transaction Pattern Analysis
description: An ongoing monitoring mechanism that assesses customer transaction patterns against normal profile baselines to identify suspicious activity. The control compares actual transaction behavior (deposits, transfers, payment types) against expected patterns for the customer's profile type.
context: Customer Risk Profile = Transaction Pattern Analysis
Normal Profile Examples: Salary deposits monthly + regular bills
Suspicious Pattern Examples: Large deposit immediately followed by international transfer

name: Customer
description: The subject of transaction pattern assessment and risk profiling. Customers are categorized by their normal transaction patterns (salary deposits, business deposits, pension payments) to establish baselines for detecting suspicious activity.
context: Customer Risk Profile = Transaction Pattern Analysis
Normal Profile Examples: Salary deposits monthly + regular bills

name: Suspicious Transaction
description: A transaction or sequence of transactions that deviates from the customer's established normal profile and triggers monitoring or investigation. Examples include large deposits immediately followed by international transfers, round-dollar amounts to multiple countries, and structuring patterns.
context: Large deposit immediately followed by international transfer
Cash deposits followed by wire transfers out

name: Deposit
description: A credit transaction to a customer account that is monitored as part of transaction pattern analysis. Deposits are assessed for consistency with the customer's normal profile, including salary deposits, savings deposits, business deposits, and pension payments.

name: Wire Transfer
description: An outbound transfer transaction, particularly international transfers, that is monitored for suspicious patterns. The document identifies wire transfers following large deposits or cash deposits as a suspicious pattern indicator.
context: Large deposit immediately followed by international transfer
Cash deposits followed by wire transfers out

name: Structuring Transaction
description: Repeated transfers deliberately kept just below reporting thresholds to evade detection and regulatory reporting obligations. This pattern is identified as a key suspicious indicator in transaction profile assessment.
context: Structuring (repeated transfers just below reporting threshold)

name: Suspicious Transaction Action Policy
description: Policy governing the bank's procedures for identifying, investigating, and responding to suspicious transactions. Establishes a four-step process from initial alert through investigation, decision-making, and documentation, with mandatory reporting obligations to the NCA.
context: System generates alert or staff observation
Suspicious Activity Report filed with NCA

name: Suspicious Transaction Alert Generation
description: Requires that suspicious transactions trigger either an automated system alert or staff observation, initiating the investigation process.
context: System generates alert or staff observation
Transaction placed on hold (up to 5 business days)

name: Transaction Hold Pending Review
description: Mandates that flagged transactions be placed on hold for up to 5 business days while the Financial Crime team conducts immediate review.
context: Transaction placed on hold (up to 5 business days)

name: Customer Explanation Request During Investigation
description: Requires the bank to contact the customer for explanation of the suspicious transaction, subject to a safety assessment to determine if contact is appropriate.
context: Customer contacted for explanation (if safe to do so)

name: Supporting Documentation Review
description: Requires review of supporting documentation and transaction history as part of the investigation process to inform risk assessment.

name: Suspicious Activity Reporting to NCA
description: Mandates filing of a Suspicious Activity Report with the National Crime Agency when suspicious activity is confirmed and the transaction is approved to proceed.
context: Suspicious Activity Report filed with NCA

name: Transaction Rejection Without AML Disclosure
description: Prohibits disclosure of AML-related reasons when declining a suspicious transaction, preventing customer awareness of the bank's suspicions.
context: Decline transaction (without informing customer of AML reason)

name: Account Freezing Pending Investigation
description: Authorizes the bank to freeze an account when a suspicious transaction requires extended investigation, blocking further activity.

name: Decision Documentation and Confidentiality
description: Requires all investigation decisions to be documented with reasoning and marked confidential, with prohibition on customer disclosure to prevent tipping off.

name: Tipping Off Prohibition
description: Prohibits disclosure to customers that their transaction or account is under AML investigation, as required by anti-money laundering legislation.

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk that customer transactions may be used to conceal the origins of illicit funds or integrate proceeds of crime into the financial system, triggering investigation and reporting obligations.
context: Suspicious Activity Report filed with NCA

name: Suspicious Transaction Activity
description: The risk that transactions may exhibit patterns or characteristics inconsistent with the customer's known profile or legitimate business purpose, requiring investigation and escalation.
context: System generates alert or staff observation

name: Automated Transaction Monitoring System
description: An automated system that generates alerts when transactions meet suspicious activity criteria, enabling rapid identification and escalation to the Financial Crime team.
context: System generates alert or staff observation
Transaction placed on hold (up to 5 business days)

name: Transaction Hold Mechanism
description: A control that suspends flagged transactions for up to 5 business days, preventing settlement while investigation proceeds.
context: Transaction placed on hold (up to 5 business days)

name: Account Freeze Control
description: A control that blocks all account activity when investigation of suspicious transactions requires extended review, preventing further transactions or withdrawals.

name: Investigation Documentation System
description: A system for recording all investigation decisions, reasoning, and outcomes with confidential marking to maintain audit trail and prevent unauthorized disclosure.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The team responsible for immediate review of suspicious transaction alerts, conducting investigations, and making decisions on whether to approve, reject, block, or file a SAR.
context: Customer contacted for explanation (if safe to do so)

name: Staff Observation Role
description: All staff members are responsible for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions that may not be caught by automated systems.
context: System generates alert or staff observation

name: National Crime Agency
description: The external regulatory authority to which Suspicious Activity Reports must be filed when the bank identifies confirmed suspicious activity.
context: Suspicious Activity Report filed with NCA

name: Suspicious Transaction
description: A financial transaction that exhibits characteristics or patterns triggering investigation under the bank's AML procedures, subject to hold, investigation, and potential reporting to the NCA.
context: Transaction placed on hold (up to 5 business days)

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing
description: The obligation to file a Suspicious Activity Report with the NCA when investigation confirms suspicious activity and the transaction is approved to proceed.
context: Suspicious Activity Report filed with NCA

name: Customer Account
description: A customer account that may be subject to transaction holds or account freezing when suspicious activity is detected during investigation.

name: Customer
description: The account holder whose transaction is under investigation and who may be contacted for explanation, subject to safety assessment and tipping off prohibitions.
context: Customer contacted for explanation (if safe to do so)

name: Suspicious Activity Reporting Policy
description: Policy governing the identification, assessment, and filing of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) to relevant authorities. Establishes mandatory and discretionary SAR filing triggers based on detection of money laundering, terrorist financing, proceeds of crime, sanctions violations, and other financial crime indicators.

name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Money Laundering Suspicion
description: Requires filing of a SAR whenever money laundering is suspected, regardless of transaction amount. This is a mandatory trigger with no discretionary threshold.

name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Terrorist Financing Suspicion
description: Requires filing of a SAR whenever terrorist financing is suspected. This is a mandatory trigger under the policy.

name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Proceeds of Crime Suspicion
description: Requires filing of a SAR when proceeds of crime under the Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA) are suspected. This is a mandatory trigger.

name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Sanctions Violation
description: Requires filing of a SAR when a sanctions violation is suspected or detected. This is a mandatory trigger.

name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Large Cash Transactions Without Clear Purpose
description: Requires filing of a SAR when large cash transactions occur with no obvious legitimate purpose. This is a mandatory trigger.
context: Large cash transactions with no obvious purpose

name: Mandatory SAR Filing When Customer Refuses Information Provision
description: Requires filing of a SAR when customers are unwilling or refuse to provide requested information. This is a mandatory trigger.

name: Mandatory SAR Filing on Detection of Structuring
description: Requires filing of a SAR when structuring is detected — the deliberate practice of breaking up transactions to avoid reporting thresholds. This is a mandatory trigger.

name: Discretionary SAR Filing on Unusual Transaction Patterns
description: Permits discretionary SAR filing when unusual transaction patterns are detected that are not clearly illegal. This is a discretionary trigger allowing staff judgment.
context: Unusual transaction patterns not clearly illegal

name: Discretionary SAR Filing on Potential Fraud
description: Permits discretionary SAR filing when potential fraud is suspected, distinct from AML-related fraud. This is a discretionary trigger.

name: Discretionary SAR Filing on Regulatory Concern
description: Permits discretionary SAR filing when a regulatory concern arises that warrants reporting. This is a discretionary trigger.

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk of customer funds or transactions being used to conceal the origins of illegally obtained money. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger in this policy.

name: Terrorist Financing
description: The risk of the bank's services being used to finance terrorist activities or organizations. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

name: Proceeds of Crime
description: The risk of handling or facilitating the movement of proceeds derived from criminal activity under the Proceeds of Crime Act. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

name: Sanctions Violation
description: The risk of conducting transactions with sanctioned individuals, entities, or jurisdictions in breach of applicable sanctions regimes. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

name: Transaction Structuring
description: The risk of customers deliberately breaking up transactions into smaller amounts to avoid triggering reporting thresholds and regulatory scrutiny. Identified as a mandatory SAR filing trigger.

name: Fraud
description: The risk of fraudulent activity on customer accounts or transactions, distinct from AML-related fraud. Identified as a discretionary SAR filing trigger.

name: SAR Filing Obligation
description: The overarching obligation to file Suspicious Activity Reports to the relevant authority when mandatory or discretionary triggers are met. Covers both mandatory and discretionary filing scenarios.

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing Process
description: The bank's formal process for preparing, approving, and submitting Suspicious Activity Reports to the NCA. The process comprises four sequential steps: report preparation with detailed narrative and risk assessment, internal approval by Compliance Head and Chief Risk Officer, submission via SARs Online within 30 days of suspicion, and follow-up cooperation with NCA investigations.
context: Filed via Suspicious Activity Report Online (SARs Online)
Filed within 30 days of suspicion arising
Bank cooperates fully with any investigation

name: SAR Filing Deadline
description: The mandatory timeframe within which a Suspicious Activity Report must be submitted to the NCA following the identification of suspicious activity. Reports must be filed within 30 days of suspicion arising.
context: Filed within 30 days of suspicion arising

name: SAR Report Preparation
description: The requirement to prepare a detailed SAR containing a narrative of suspicious activity, transaction timeline, customer and transaction details, supporting evidence, risk assessment, and a recommendation regarding suspected money laundering or terrorist financing.
context: Recommendation (ML suspected, TF suspected, or other)

name: SAR Internal Approval Gate
description: The mandatory internal approval process requiring Compliance Head review and approval, Chief Risk Officer sign-off for significant cases, and CEO notification for high-profile reports before submission to the NCA.

name: SAR NCA Submission Requirement
description: The obligation to file Suspicious Activity Reports to the NCA via the SARs Online system within 30 days of suspicion arising, with confirmation of submission by the NCA.
context: Filed via Suspicious Activity Report Online (SARs Online)
Filed within 30 days of suspicion arising

name: SAR Follow-Up and Cooperation
description: The requirement for the bank to cooperate fully with NCA requests for additional information and investigations following SAR submission, and to retain all supporting documentation for a minimum of 5 years.
context: Bank cooperates fully with any investigation

name: SAR Document Retention
description: The mandatory requirement to retain all Suspicious Activity Report documentation and supporting evidence for a minimum of 5 years following submission.

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk of money laundering identified through suspicious activity, which triggers the requirement to prepare and file a Suspicious Activity Report with a recommendation of suspected ML.
context: Recommendation (ML suspected, TF suspected, or other)

name: Terrorist Financing
description: The risk of terrorist financing identified through suspicious activity, which triggers the requirement to prepare and file a Suspicious Activity Report with a recommendation of suspected TF.
context: Recommendation (ML suspected, TF suspected, or other)

name: Compliance Head
description: The role responsible for reviewing and approving Suspicious Activity Reports before submission to the NCA as part of the internal approval gate.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: The role responsible for providing sign-off on significant Suspicious Activity Reports as part of the internal approval process.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: The role responsible for notification in cases of high-profile Suspicious Activity Reports as part of the internal approval process.

name: National Crime Agency
description: The external regulatory authority to which Suspicious Activity Reports are filed via the SARs Online system. The NCA confirms receipt of submissions and may request additional information or conduct investigations.
context: Filed via Suspicious Activity Report Online (SARs Online)

name: Suspicious Activity Report Online System
description: The online system used by the bank to file Suspicious Activity Reports to the NCA. Reports must be submitted via this system within 30 days of suspicion arising.
context: Filed via Suspicious Activity Report Online (SARs Online)

name: SAR Confidentiality Policy
description: Policy governing the confidentiality of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and prohibiting the disclosure of SAR filings or grounds for suspicion to customers. The policy establishes a strict tipping off prohibition with criminal and regulatory consequences for breach.
context: Do not inform customer of SAR filing
Cannot tell customer a SAR has been filed

name: Prohibition on Customer Notification of SAR Filing
description: Mandatory prohibition preventing staff from informing customers that a Suspicious Activity Report has been filed against their account or transaction.
context: Cannot tell customer a SAR has been filed
Do not inform customer of SAR filing

name: Prohibition on Disclosure of Grounds for Suspicion
description: Mandatory prohibition preventing staff from disclosing to customers the grounds, reasons, or basis for suspicion that triggered a SAR filing.

name: Prohibition on Description of Suspicious Transactions
description: Mandatory prohibition preventing staff from describing to customers the specific transactions or activities that were identified as suspicious and reported in a SAR.

name: Prohibition on Transaction Delay for SAR Preparation with Customer Notification
description: Mandatory prohibition preventing staff from delaying a customer transaction in order to prepare and file a SAR, and then subsequently informing the customer of the delay or SAR filing.
context: Cannot delay transaction to prepare SAR and then inform customer

name: Exception to Tipping Off Prohibition for Normal Transaction Processing
description: Provision establishing that communication with a customer regarding a transaction is not considered tipping off when the SAR has already been filed and the transaction is proceeding normally without delay or special handling.
context: SAR already filed and transaction proceeding normally (communication not tipping off)

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk of customer involvement in money laundering activities, which triggers the obligation to file a Suspicious Activity Report and maintain strict confidentiality regarding the filing and grounds for suspicion.

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing Obligation
description: The obligation to file a Suspicious Activity Report when grounds for suspicion exist, coupled with the strict requirement to maintain confidentiality of the filing and not disclose it to the customer.
context: Do not inform customer of SAR filing
Cannot tell customer a SAR has been filed
SAR already filed and transaction proceeding normally

name: All Staff
description: All bank staff members are responsible for adhering to the SAR confidentiality and tipping off prohibition requirements. Breach of these obligations carries criminal, regulatory, and disciplinary consequences including potential termination.

name: European Union Consolidated Sanctions List

description: The risk that the bank may engage in transactions with sanctioned entities, individuals, or jurisdictions in violation of OFAC, EU, HMT, or UN sanctions programs. This is a primary compliance risk addressed through sanctions screening.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: Ongoing screening process against multiple sanctions lists including OFAC, EU, HMT, and UN designations. The bank monitors customers, transactions, and counterparties against these lists to prevent sanctions violations.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: Mandatory screening process requiring customer names to be checked against all sanctions lists with real-time updates, supplemented by screening of immediate family and associates. Includes transaction screening for high-risk jurisdictions and hit processing procedures with account freeze and NCA escalation protocols.
context: Customer name checked against all lists

name: Sanctions List Screening at Customer Onboarding
description: Mandatory requirement to check customer names against all sanctions lists with real-time updates and supplementary screening of immediate family and associates.
context: Customer name checked against all lists

name: Transaction Screening for High-Risk Jurisdictions
description: Mandatory requirement to screen all transactions for activity involving high-risk jurisdictions as part of ongoing sanctions compliance.

name: Immediate Account Freeze on Potential Sanctions Match
description: Mandatory requirement to immediately freeze an account upon detection of a potential match against sanctions lists, pending manual review and false positive assessment.
context: Manual review of match (false positive assessment)

name: Escalation to Compliance Head and NCA Notice Filing on True Hit
description: Mandatory requirement to escalate confirmed sanctions matches to the Compliance Head and immediately file a notice with the National Crime Agency (NCA) upon confirmation of a true hit.
context: If true hit = escalate to Compliance Head + immediately file NCA notice

name: Account Remains Blocked Pending Resolution

name: No Transactions Permitted on Blocked Account

name: Asset Freeze on Blocked Account
description: Mandatory requirement to implement asset freeze on blocked accounts to prevent removal of funds pending resolution of sanctions matter.

name: Confidentiality of Sanctions Block Reason from Customer
description: Prohibition on informing the customer of the reason for account freeze or sanctions block, maintaining confidentiality of the screening match and investigation.

name: NCA Notification via Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation
description: Mandatory requirement to notify the National Crime Agency through the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) of confirmed sanctions matches and blocked accounts.

name: Sanctions Violation
description: Risk of customer or transaction involvement with sanctioned individuals, entities, or high-risk jurisdictions, exposing the bank to regulatory penalties, criminal liability, and reputational harm.
context: Customer name checked against all lists

name: Real-Time Sanctions List Update Mechanism
description: Operational control ensuring that sanctions screening lists are updated in real-time as lists change daily, maintaining current coverage of sanctioned entities and individuals.

name: Supplementary Screening of Family and Associates
description: Operational control requiring screening of immediate family members and associates of customers against sanctions lists to identify indirect sanctions evasion attempts.

name: Manual False Positive Assessment Process

name: Compliance Head

name: High-Risk Jurisdiction Beneficial Ownership
